newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices flat to up 1/8 pt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices flat to up 1/8 pt.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were even to up 1/8 point at midday, as prices recovered from data-induced morning softness.
"They are moving in synch with govies right now," one trader said, adding that trading was light. "I'd say we are firm to up 1/8 of a point or so."
Muni prices dipped about 1/4 point in early trade following release of economic data on inflation and employment.

The Labor Department said the consumer price index for April rose 0.1 percent, and increased 0.3 percent at the core. The figure was almost in line with economists' expectations, which pegged the overall figure at up 0.1 percent and 0.2 percent higher at the core.
The Department also released initial jobless claims for the week ended May 10, which fell to 319,000.

"It seemed like people wanted to buy when (the muni market) was down, and nothing really traded although there were bids that were probably down about 3/8," one trader said. "But as soon as the market popped back up, bids improved, and maybe some things are up 1/8," the trader said. "At worse case they are unch'ed."
Prices began to make up some ground later Thursday morning.
"I think industrial production and capacity utilization helped," a trader said.

The Federal Reserve's industrial production figure April, which was unchanged from March and below the expectations of a 0.2 percent rise. Capacity utilization was 83.4 percent, compared to expectations for 84.1 percent.
Also Thursday, the Philadelphia Fed said its business activity index was 1.6 in May, versus 5.7 in April.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract was up 8/32 at 116-10/32. The June T-bond contract was up 5/32 at 110-10/32. The MOB spread was 192 ticks.
The benchmark 30-year bond was up 5/32 at 96-28/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
In new issue action, Prudential Securities Inc said it won $60 million of Montgomery County, Pa., general obligation bonds at a true interest cost of 5.3975 percent.
On the negotiated side, Smith Barney Inc tentatively priced $37 million Oregon State Board of Higher Education bonds to yield 5.65 percent in 2027.
